title: Show HN: TrnRT – An open-source LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium
snippet:
Hi HN, Sanchit here from RunAnywhere (YC W26). We just open-sourced TrnRT: Trainium RunTime, our inference engine for AWS Trainium. We started 3 weeks back, and currently we’re able to serve and run GLM 5.3 flash (FP8) on AWS trn2.48xlarge, and will bring more models support soon. It’s open to contributions :)
What it does today:
- Serves 2 instances of GLM-5.3 flash on a single box, 8 trn2 with a cache aware router.
- Can process 3.57M TPM (tokens per minute) on SemiAnalysis's AgentX benchmarks

title: LoCaR: Localized Canvas Retrieval With Frozen Vision-Language Model
snippet:
arXiv:2611.22131v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whole image embeddings can under represent small objects and local attributes that distinguish relevant images for localized queries. We present LoCaR, a training free framework for localized text to image retrieval with frozen vision language models. LoCaR constructs and utilizes independent proposals (SAM2) focusing on the object so as to get a more localized representation that independently encodes each region using the frozen visual encoder.

snippet:

Abstract: Tool-augmented medical agents treat whatever their tools return as evidence. title: The Fragility of Reasoning-Importance Attribution for Pruning Language Models
snippet:
arXiv:2611.22234v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attribution-guided pruning scores components by their causal contribution and protects the important ones, and it is increasingly applied to compress reasoning language models without destroying their chain of thought. Its reliability rests on an unexamined assumption: that reasoning importance can be faithfully measured. Across four small reasoning models, we show this measurement is fragile in three ways, each of which changes pruning decisions.
